definition: A filter in a diesel exhaust that traps soot. Lots of short trips clog it, and cleaning or replacing it is costly.
Sends some exhaust gas back into the engine to cut emissions. Over time it clogs with soot.
Volkswagen's automatic gearbox with two clutches. Quick and smooth, but it needs oil changes on time.
An automatic gearbox that uses two clutches for fast gear changes. Repairs can be expensive.
Audi's name for its dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
The electronic control unit inside an automatic gearbox that works the gears. Costly if it fails.
An automatic gearbox with no fixed gears. Smooth, but its fluid must be changed on time.
The simple gearbox in Toyota hybrids. Very reliable, and not the same as a normal CVT.
Audi's older CVT automatic gearbox. Known for costly failures, especially without fluid changes.
Honda's automated manual gearbox. A small motor works the clutch, and that motor can fail.
A traditional automatic gearbox design. Usually smooth and long-lasting with fluid changes.
The single gear in an electric car that does the job of a gearbox.
A rubber belt that keeps the engine's valves and pistons in step. If it snaps, the engine can be ruined.
A timing belt that runs in engine oil. As it breaks up, bits can block the oil supply.
A metal chain doing the timing belt's job. Meant to last, but some stretch, rattle and need replacing.
Keeps a timing chain or belt tight. When it wears, the chain can rattle or jump a tooth.
A heavy disc between engine and clutch that smooths vibration. It wears and is usually replaced with the clutch.
A small fan driven by exhaust gas that pushes extra air into the engine for more power.
A small valve on the turbo that controls boost. When worn it rattles and power can drop.
The pipe carrying pressurised air from the turbo. If it splits, power drops suddenly.
Sprays fuel into the engine. A faulty one causes rough running, smoke or higher fuel use.
A fast, precise type of diesel injector. Accurate, but expensive to replace.
Feeds fuel at very high pressure to the injectors. When it fails, the engine stalls or loses power.
Small heaters that help a diesel start in the cold. Faulty ones cause hard starts and smoke.
A liquid added to modern diesel exhausts to cut pollution. Its tank, pump and sensors can fail.
Measures pollution in the exhaust. When it fails, a warning light comes on and power may be limited.
A small valve that vents gases from inside the engine. When it fails, oil use and rough idle can follow.
Valves that let air into the engine. On direct-injection engines carbon builds up on them over time.
Cleaning carbon off intake valves by blasting them with crushed walnut shells.
Small flaps in a diesel's air intake. Their motor can fail and, rarely, a flap breaks off.
Toyota's system that varies how far the valves open. Its controller can fail and light the engine warning.
The small gap at each engine valve. Some engines need it checked and adjusted at services.
When a cylinder fails to fire properly. The engine shakes or stumbles and the engine light may come on.
A safety mode that cuts power when the car detects a fault, so you can drive slowly to a garage.
Pumps oil around the engine. If it stops working, the engine can be destroyed within seconds.
A spinning shaft that cancels engine vibration. On some engines it also drives the oil pump.
Fuel gets into the engine oil, often on short trips. It thins the oil and wears the engine faster.
The top part of the engine that holds the valves. A cracked head means a big repair.
The seal between engine block and head. If it fails, coolant leaks or mixes with oil and it overheats.
The liquid that stops the engine overheating. Losing it with no visible leak is a warning sign.
The plastic coolant tank under the bonnet. Check the level sits between the MIN and MAX marks.
Pumps coolant around the engine. A leak or failure can make the engine overheat.
A valve that controls engine temperature. It or its plastic housing can start leaking coolant.
A rubber-mounted ring at the front of the engine that absorbs vibration. If it breaks up, belts get damaged.
A rubber block holding the engine in place. When worn you feel vibration and clunks.
A parking brake worked by a button and small motors on the rear brakes. The motors can fail.
ABS stops the wheels locking under hard braking; ESP helps stop skids. A warning light means it is off.
A suspension link between wheel and body. Worn ones cause knocks and vague steering.
A metal frame under the car that carries the suspension. Heavy rust there is a serious problem.
Lets a wheel spin smoothly. A worn one hums or rumbles, louder as you go faster.
Suspension that uses air bags instead of steel springs. Comfortable, but leaks are common with age.
The large battery that powers a hybrid's electric motor. It wears slowly; replacing it is costly.
The small ordinary battery that powers the electronics. In hybrids and EVs a weak one stops the car starting.
Converts battery power for the electric motor in hybrids and EVs. It has its own coolant pump.
An efficient electric heater in EVs. Saves range in winter, but a fault leaves the cabin cold.
The part of an EV that charges the battery from a home socket or AC charger. If it fails, AC charging stops.
When the driver-assist system brakes hard for no real reason.
A free repair the manufacturer orders for a known fault. Ask for proof it was done.
The car's unique 17-character ID. Use it to check mileage, accident history and recalls.
The record of the car's services. Stamps and invoices show it was looked after.
Lithuania's compulsory roadworthiness test (TA). A valid one means the car recently passed basic checks.
A small gearbox that sends power to the rear axle on AWD cars. It needs fresh oil or it wears out.
The clutch that connects the rear wheels on many AWD cars. Its pump fails if the oil is not changed.
The electronic board inside a Mercedes automatic gearbox. When it fails, the car gets stuck in one gear.
A part that changes valve timing. When worn it rattles on cold starts and turns on the engine light.
Rings that seal the pistons. When they stick or wear, the engine burns oil.
A soot filter on newer petrol engines, like a diesel DPF. Short trips can clog it.
Ford's dual-clutch automatic. Dry-clutch versions are known for shuddering and early failures.
The engine burns off soot in the DPF by running hotter, usually on longer drives. Short trips interrupt it.
Hybrids and EVs slow down by charging the battery, so the normal brakes are used less and can rust.
The valve that controls how much air enters a petrol engine. Dirt makes it stick and the idle unstable.
Makes the high voltage for a spark plug. A failing coil causes misfires and a shaking engine.
An electric valve that controls oil flow inside an automatic gearbox. Faulty ones cause harsh or late shifts.
Changing engine software for more power. It adds stress to the turbo, clutch and gearbox.
A swivel joint in the suspension. When worn it creaks or knocks over bumps.
An older fast-charging plug used by the Nissan Leaf. Fewer new chargers support it.
How much of an EV battery's original capacity is left. Lower health means less range.
A phone app that reads a Nissan Leaf's battery health through a cheap OBD adapter.
